description: Watershed Workflow is a Python toolset developed largely at Oak Ridge National Laboratory for preparing data-intensive hydrological simulations. It retrieves and combines watershed boundaries, river networks, elevation, land cover, soils and meteorological data, then generates meshes and associated model inputs. Coverage centres on the conterminous United States, with the README describing substantial support for Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico. Source is free under BSD-3-Clause. A limitation is that coverage differs by upstream data service, some network workflows need service credentials, and Windows support is less tested than Linux or macOS. Users must check the resulting mesh and parameter choices before running a hydrological solver. The toolset can prepare reservoir, flood and water-availability simulations. Wflow (model-wflow) is related hydrological modelling context, without a verified direct mesh interface. The 2022 methods citation and README were inspected. No geospatial data or mesh archive was downloaded.
